transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-12
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording ID: ff-20250512-omega-8742
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM), Michael Chen (Omega Head of Platform), Sara López (Omega Security Eng), Dev Patel (Identity Eng), Anna Weiss (Omega GRC)

Summary:
Quick security and provisioning review for SSO/SCIM, and alignment on RBAC/least-privilege mapping and KMS/BYOK requirements. Customer has Okta and Azure AD in use, wants SCIM for provisioning and group sync, expects audit logs export and 1yr retention, and is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for data residency.

Topics covered:
- SAML metadata exchange and ACS/Entity config
- SCIM provisioning behavior (full-sync vs delta, group sync edge cases)
- Mapping groups -> Redwood roles and least-privilege model recommendations
- Audit logs: events captured, retention, export formats (JSON/CSV), SIEM integration
- Encryption and BYOK: options for AWS KMS and HSM-backed keys, key rotation
- Data residency and private control plane considerations

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Alex Morgan, AE at Redwood, I'm here with Priya our SE, Jordan our CSM. How's everybody doing?
[00:07] Michael: Good, thanks. We wanted to get through SSO, SCIM, and the role mapping today, mostly from a security gating perspective. We've got some legal asks too.
[00:14] Alex: Great. Priya, do you want to lead the SSO/SCIM walkthrough?
[00:18] Priya: Sure. I'll start at a high level, then we'll dig into the SCIM specifics and RBAC mapping. Quick note: Omega mentioned they're on Okta for most teams, but Azure AD for a few business units, so we should cover both IdP flows.
[00:29] Dev: Correct, Okta is our primary IdP. We also have a small Azure tenant we need to support. We prefer SCIM provisioning for automating deprovisioning since onboarding is frequent.
[00:39] Priya: Understood. For SAML, Redwood supports standard entity metadata exchange. We'll provide an SP metadata XML with ACS URL, entityID, and a recommended NameID format (email). Okta's straightforward, for Azure there's a slightly different claim config.
[00:52] Sara: For NameID, we need email as persistent. We have a few users where email normalization is weird, so mapping rules are important. Also interested in SCIM attribute mapping for department and groups.
[01:02] Priya: We'll include attribute-mapping examples. SCIM supports groups and user attributes; our SCIM endpoint supports bulk operations and incremental delta syncs via changedAt. We do also support group membership syncing but there are limits for very large groups (we'll note paging thresholds).
[01:20] Michael: On provisioning, we care about deprovisioning - when HR marks someone terminated in Okta, we want Redwood to revoke access within 5 minutes. Is that realistic?
[01:30] Priya: SCIM push events are near real-time; in practice from IdP to Redwood depends on polling vs push webhook config. With Okta SCIM app connector set to 1 minute polling and our SCIM scaffolding, sub-5 minute deprovisioning is achievable, but we should validate in a live test.
[01:42] Dev: We do rely on the delta sync field; does Redwood honor externalId and canonical user id from SCIM?
[01:48] Priya: Yes, we support externalId and the id fields, and we try to match by username/email then externalId. We'll document precedence in the mapping sheet.
[01:56] Alex: Quick note - we'll send a SCIM mapping spreadsheet that shows recommended group->role mappings.
[02:00] Anna: On roles, our GRC wants a least-privilege model: a handful of roles (viewer, operator, admin) with clearly defined permissions and audited role changes. Can you show how Redwood's RBAC maps to groups?
[02:12] Priya: Sure. Our recommended pattern: use SCIM groups named for the role (e.g., redwood-admins, redwood-ops, redwood-readonly). On user provisioning we map group membership to Redwood roles. Role changes via SCIM or the Console both generate audit events.
[02:28] Sara: Is there a way to prevent self-promotion? Like a user who is in an admin group in Okta shouldn't be able to add themselves to the group in Redwood.
[02:36] Priya: Yes, role assignment is enforced by SCIM/group membership from IdP or by Console actions gated by RBAC. Console UI respects least privilege; only users with admin role can change group mappings. We'll show how to lock down the OAuth tokens and service accounts for SCIM.
[02:49] Michael: Let's talk audit logs and retention. We need 12 months of immutable logs and the ability to export to our SIEM. What events do you capture?
[02:58] Priya: We capture auth events (SAML assertion accepted/rejected), provisioning changes (SCIM create/update/delete), role changes, model invocation metadata at route level (not user prompt content unless you enable ingestion), and admin console changes. Logs are available via API and S3 export in JSON/CSV. Retention in Hosted is 90 days by default, but Dedicated/Private can extend to 1 year or longer per contract.
[03:18] Anna: For SOC 2 evidence, do you provide log retention and integrity proofs?
[03:22] Jordan: We provide exportable logs and signed delivery for audit; for dedicated/private customers we can integrate with your KMS and more stringent retention. We'll also share our SOC 2 report under NDA.
[03:31] Sara: Encryption: we want BYOK for keys and HSM-backed if possible. Are keys customer-managed?
[03:36] Priya: Hosted supports cloud KMS options (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) with customer-managed keys; Dedicated/Private can do HSM or on-prem key stores. We support envelope encryption where the model payloads are encrypted with a data key wrapped by your KMS key. Key rotation is supported but you'll need to coordinate rotation windows.
[03:52] Michael: Data residency: some accounts need EU-only processing. Can we pin those to eu-central region and ensure no cross-region replication?
[03:59] Priya: Yes, with Private or Dedicated you can enforce region pinning and network egress rules. Hosted supports region selection for storage/compute but for strict EU-only legal controls we'd recommend Private. We'll outline tradeoffs in the follow-up doc.
[04:12] Dev: A couple of nitty-gritty questions: what is the SCIM schema version, do you support group nested membership, and are there rate limits we need to be aware of when Okta pushes bulk updates?
[04:22] Priya: We support SCIM 2.0; nested groups are not first-class, we flatten membership for role mapping and document behavior if you use nested groups. Rate limits: our SCIM endpoint supports burst for provisioning but we recommend batching large imports via our bulk import API to avoid throttles. We'll put precise limits in the doc.
[04:40] Sara: For SAML signature and encryption, what's the algorithm you require? SHA256 is fine?
[04:44] Priya: SHA256 for signatures is recommended; we also accept RSA-SHA256. For assertion encryption we support AES256. We'll include an example metadata XML.
[04:54] Michael: How about session timeouts and remember-me? Our security team wants short sessions for admin roles.
[05:00] Priya: Admin sessions default to 30 minutes of inactivity, with refresh tokens for longer lived service accounts. Session configs are customizable for Dedicated/Private.
[05:10] Alex: Are there any blockers from Redwood side for integrating with Okta and Azure AD?
[05:13] Priya: No blockers. We typically exchange metadata files, configure SCIM app on Okta/Azure, and run a test user provisioning. For Azure there are claim-mapping gotchas we'll call out.
[05:24] Dev: For lifecycle deprovisioning test, do you want us to create a sandbox Okta app or can you provide a test tenant?
[05:30] Alex: We can spin up a Redwood test tenant for provisioning tests; we prefer you provide a sandbox Okta or test account so you can control the HR lifecycle events.
[05:39] Anna: On the SOC 2 front, we need a copy of your current report before procurement sign-off.
[05:44] Jordan: We'll send the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. Also we'll attach our standard security pack and the SOC compliance FAQ.
[05:51] Sara: For audit logging, do you produce tamper-evident logs or signed hashes? That's a requirement for some audits.
[05:58] Priya: We can produce signed log bundles for Dedicated/Private, including hash chains to show integrity. For Hosted we provide exportable logs and signed delivery on request as part of an enterprise package.
[06:09] Michael: Ok great. Any specific RBAC best practices you recommend for finance orgs?
[06:15] Priya: Keep admin roles minimal, separate duties (admin vs billing vs devops), use ephemeral admin sessions where possible, enforce MFA on admin accounts, and prefer group-based assignments instead of individual role grants. We'll show a recommended role matrix in the mapping sheet.
[06:30] Dev: How do you handle service accounts for automation that need elevated privileges?
[06:34] Priya: Service accounts get their own scoped tokens; we recommend creating least-privilege service roles and rotating service credentials regularly. For SCIM we use client credentials for the connector with limited scopes.
[06:44] Michael: Any compliance features around data access logs tied to prompts or PII?
[06:50] Priya: By default we redact or don't persist full prompt text for standard plans; for privacy-sensitive customers we support filtered telemetry and PII suppression. If you need full logging for debugging we recommend separating that flow into a secure project and restricting access.
[07:03] Anna: Let's recap next steps.
[07:06] Alex: Recap: we will send the SAML and SCIM docs, mapping sheet, SOC 2 report under NDA, and propose a live provisioning test next week. Michael and team will share role lists and sandbox Okta details.
[07:18] Michael: That works. One more thing - can you also confirm the exact events written to audit logs during provisioning? We need that for our security questionnaire.
[07:26] Priya: Yes we'll include a log event table: create/update/delete user, group membership changes, SAML auth attempt, token issuance, admin console changes, role change events with actor and timestamp.
[07:37] Dev: Sounds good. We'll aim to have the sandbox ready by Wed.
[07:41] Alex: Great. We'll follow up via email and upload docs to the DealRoom. Thanks everyone.
[07:46] Jordan: Thanks all, closing notes: action items and we'll track in the CRM.
[07:50] (end of recording)

Notes on transcription quality: some names may be slightly mis-transcribed, e.g., GRC vs G-R-C, and there may be dropped filler words; timestamps are approximate.
